title: Derived ringed-topos counit under coefficient restriction
statement:
Let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y)$ be a morphism of topoi presented by small sites [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $A_X,A_Y$ be its constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and identify $f^{-1}A_Y=A_X$. Let $R_X,R_Y$ be sheaves of commutative $A_X,A_Y$-algebras, with a compatible structural map $c:f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$. Write $D(A_W),D(R_W)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and $U_W:D(R_W)\to D(A_W)$ for exact coefficient restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $Q_A=f^{-1}$ on constant-$A$ complexes and $Q_R=Lf_R^*$ be derived module pullback along $c$, computed with flat-term K-flat resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Let $F_A=Rf_{*,A}$ and $F_R=Rf_{*,R}$ be K-injective derived direct images, with the canonical derived module adjunctions and counits $\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_R$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows].

Let $\kappa:U_YF_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F_AU_X$ be the canonical comparison of the two factorizations of $(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X),R_X)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y),A_Y)$, normalized by the K-injective derived-composition maps of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Let $\tau:Q_AU_Y\to U_XQ_R$ be the canonical scalar-unit comparison: for a flat-term K-flat $R_Y$-complex $P$ it is the class of the degreewise map $f^{-1}U_YP\to U_X(R_X\otimes_{f^{-1}R_Y}f^{-1}P)$ sending $x$ to $1\otimes x$, with the canonical resolution identifications. Then for every $K\in D(R_X)$ one has the equality in $D(A_X)$
$$U_X(\varepsilon_{R,K})\circ\tau_{F_RK}=\varepsilon_{A,U_XK}\circ Q_A(\kappa_K).$$
The comparisons are natural in $K$ and in compatible homomorphisms of the $A$-algebra sheaves. No boundedness, flatness of $A_W\to R_W$, adic completeness, or constructibility hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Agent consequence of Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition) and Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), with the ordinary tensor adjunction of Tag 03D7 (sites-modules, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules): counit normalization for the two factorizations through constant coefficients.

proof.text: Construct $\tau$. Restriction of scalars $U_W$ is exact and is applied termwise [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Since $f^{-1}A_Y=A_X$, the module pullback for $(f,A_Y\to A_X)$ is $A_X\otimes_{A_X}f^{-1}M=f^{-1}M$, which is exact, so $Q_A$ is computed termwise on every complex. Every $R_Y$-complex admits a quasi-isomorphism from a flat-term K-flat complex [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and $Q_R$ is computed by $u^*P=R_X\otimes_{f^{-1}R_Y}f^{-1}P$ on such $P$, termwise pullback sending quasi-isomorphisms between such complexes to quasi-isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For such $P$ the degreewise map $f^{-1}U_YP\to U_X(R_X\otimes_{f^{-1}R_Y}f^{-1}P)$, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, is $A_X$-linear because $c$ is a map of $A_X$-algebras, commutes with the differentials, and is natural in chain maps $P\to P'$. Hence, composed with the canonical resolution isomorphisms $Q_R(QP)\cong Q(u^*P)$ of the last two citations, it defines a natural transformation $\tau:Q_AU_Y\to U_XQ_R$ on $D(R_Y)$, independent of the resolution because any two flat-term K-flat resolutions are compared by these natural isomorphisms. No flatness of $A_W\to R_W$ is used.

source.place: Tag 03D7, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; derived change of rings and tensor-pullback normalization

proof.text: Factor the composite ringed-topos morphism through the constant coefficient ring: first use the identity underlying topos on X with structural map $A_X\to R_X$, then use f with the constant rings $A_X,A_Y$.  The composite direct image on module sheaves is therefore the same underlying functor as $U_YF_R$, while the two successive direct images are $F_AU_X$.  The normalized K-injective comparison for a composite ringed-topos morphism supplies a natural isomorphism $\kappa:U_YF_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F_AU_X$; its normalization is exactly the class specified in the item.  Exactness of restriction of scalars lets these abelian factorizations descend termwise before taking the derived direct images.

Representative of $\varphi=U_X(\varepsilon_{R,K})\circ\tau_{F_RK}$. Let $K\in D(R_X)$, represented by a K-injective complex $I$ [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], so $F_RK$ is represented by $f_*I$. Choose a quasi-isomorphism $q:P\to f_*I$ from a flat-term K-flat $R_Y$-complex [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and let $e:f^{-1}f_*I\to I$ be the ordinary counit of $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ on underlying sheaves. The derived adjunction $Q_R\dashv F_R$ is the canonical one of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows], i.e. the bijection of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general]; its characterization with $s=\mathrm{id}_I$, $t=q$ and $f=q$ (so the left side is the identity of $F_RK$) and the module-adjunction formula of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] shows that, under $Q_RF_RK\cong Q(R_X\otimes_{f^{-1}R_Y}f^{-1}P)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], $\varepsilon_{R,K}$ is the class of $s\otimes x\mapsto s\,e(f^{-1}q(x))$. Precomposing with $\tau$ ($x\mapsto1\otimes x$) gives $e\circ f^{-1}(q)$. Since $f^{-1}(q)$ is a quasi-isomorphism ($f^{-1}$ exact), under $Q_AU_YF_RK=Q(f^{-1}U_Yf_*I)$ one gets $\varphi=Q(e)$, the class of the underlying abelian counit.

source.place: Tag 03D7, explicit tensor adjunction; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0D6E and 07A6, normalization on K-injective representatives

proof.text: The $Q_A\dashv F_A$ adjunct of $\varphi$ is $\kappa_K$. Keep $I$ from the previous step and choose a K-injective resolution $j:U_XI\to J$ of $A_X$-complexes [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; $F_AU_XK$ is represented by $f_*J$. The ordinary adjunct of the chain map $j\circ e:f^{-1}U_Yf_*I\to J$ under $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ is $f_*(j\circ e)\circ\eta_{f_*I}=f_*(j)$, by the triangle identity of the abelian adjunction. Apply the characterization of the canonical derived adjunction $Q_A\dashv F_A$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows, lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] with $s=j$, $t=\mathrm{id}$ (no left resolution is needed since $f^{-1}$ is exact): the class $Q(f_*j)$ corresponds to $Q(j)^{-1}\circ Q(j\circ e)=Q(e)=\varphi$. Now factor the composite ringed-topos morphism as in Step 2: $(\mathrm{id}_X,A_X\to R_X)$, whose direct image is $U_X$ and sends the K-injective $I$ to $U_XI$, followed by $(f,A)$. The normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] says that the class of $f_*(j):U_Yf_*I\to f_*J$ is exactly $\kappa_K$. Hence $\kappa_K$ is the $Q_A\dashv F_A$ adjunct of $\varphi$, i.e. $\kappa_K=F_A(\varphi)\circ\eta_{A,U_YF_RK}$. The identifications used are the canonical resolution isomorphisms, which are natural in $K$ by the functoriality clauses of the cited adjunction and composition statements, so the equality holds for every $K$ and is independent of the choices of $I,q,j$.

source.place: Tag 03D7, explicit tensor adjunction; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0D6E and 07A6, normalization on K-injective representatives

proof.text:
Apply the adjunct-counit identity [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] to the adjunction $Q_A\dashv F_A$, with objects $U_YF_RK$ of $D(A_Y)$ and $U_XK$ of $D(A_X)$, $\psi=\kappa_K$ and $\varphi=U_X(\varepsilon_{R,K})\circ\tau_{F_RK}$. Step 4 says $\psi=F_A(\varphi)\circ\eta_{A,U_YF_RK}$, so the identity gives
$$\varepsilon_{A,U_XK}\circ Q_A(\kappa_K)=U_X(\varepsilon_{R,K})\circ\tau_{F_RK}.$$
Naturality: $\tau$ is natural by Step 1, $\kappa$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], the counits by the derived adjunctions. For a compatible map of $A$-algebra sheaves $R\to R'$ (on $X$ and $Y$), the degreewise formula $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, the abelian counit $e$ and the representative $f_*(j)$ of Steps 3--4 are the same underlying maps for $R$ and $R'$ after restriction of scalars, so the comparisons are compatible with the restriction functors. No boundedness, flatness, completeness or constructibility hypothesis enters.
